claim: When you invoke a durable function asynchronously, the durable execution timeout can be up to 1 year; the retention period for history and checkpoint data after the execution reaches a terminal state is up to 90 days.

qualifiers.condition: the one-year execution timeout applies when the durable function is invoked asynchronously

evidence.quote: The execution timeout (up to 1 year) governs how long an execution can run. The retention period (up to 90 days) governs how long history and checkpoint data are retained after the execution reaches a terminal state.

When you invoke durable functions asynchronously, the durable execution timeout can extend up to one year, enabling use cases such as human-approval workflows, scheduled reminders, and multi-day processing pipelines.
